cache_read_weight.why: the pooled fit puts a cache read at 0.0106 of the Opus input rate, 80% interval [0.0085, 0.0135], which reaches zero or is too wide to publish as a value; the point estimate is used only inside the before-and-after comparison, with the rest of the fit.

measured_rates.method: credits_s = sum over families of rate_f x (input + cache_write + 5x output)_f,s + w x cache_reads_s, with Opus at 1 and every other rate and w free and positive; one set of rates for every account and side of 2026-09-14, and one credits-per-1% scale per account and side. Minimises, over the rates, the sum over groups and their stretches of (log(credits_s / delta_pct_s) minus that group's mean of it) squared: the group's scale is the mean, so it is never a parameter. Nelder-Mead in log space, numpy only. The rates are then read in credits against the Opus anchor, 0.6667 credits per token. Intervals are 80% bootstrap intervals over stretches resampled within each group. A family is published when its interval starts above zero and its high end is under 1.5x its low end; a family in fewer than 3 of the stretches is held at its inferred rate and not measured. A family that is not measurable carries an `inferred` rate -- the reference table's, or its list-price ratio to Opus where the table has no row -- which the page shows marked as inferred. Stretches that span the cut are in neither group.

window_credits.current_method: Every provisional or measured change of the four-account detector (`four_accounts`) opens a regime at its own instant; nothing else does, and a candidate never does. A regime opened by a provisional change is a provisional level (`provisional`). Each regime is measured in the family actually in use: its regime family is the family with the most pure clean stretches starting in it (`regime_family`, `n_regime_family`). Regimes joined by a change whose five-hour size holds no change form one run, and a run of two or more whose pure clean stretches hold 5 readings of its most common family is stated by that one cluster (`unmeasured_boundary_run_cluster`). Otherwise a regime with 5 readings is their median tokens per 1% times 100 (`measured_value`, no rate in it); below that it is the previous regime times the change's five-hour size where that size excludes no change (`previous_regime_scaled_by_known_date_change`), else the previous regime carried (`previous_regime_carried_fit_not_separable`). The published value is the newest regime's. Every earlier regime's `value` is then the next one's over the detector's five-hour size at the change between them (carried where that size holds no change), so the chart's every step is the detector's own figure; the regime's own reading stays as `own_value`. Changes applied: from 2026-09-14T09:00:00+00:00, five-hour carried; from 2026-09-23T13:00:00+00:00, five-hour +20.4%; from 2026-10-09T16:00:00+00:00, five-hour +17%.
window_credits.method: median credits per 1% of the five-hour meter over the current side of the pure-opus cluster taken from every watched account's passive stretch file, times 100 (`current_method` for which side that is). A stretch counts when it moved the meter at least 3%, carries tokens, does not overlap one of the tracker's own runs on its own account (a probe row or the effort-matrix run), and reads capture_status 'accepted'. The Max account 1 counts from 6 September, as its seven-day steps do. Every token in a pure-opus stretch is priced at a rate data/prices.json publishes, so the figure carries no fitted parameter. Cache writes at the input rate, cache reads at 0 of it.

window_credits_from_weekly.status: retired 2026-10-23: it paired the announced 14 September weekly caps with the windows-per-week regimes either side of a hand-dated cut; regimes now open only at the four-account detector's measured changes (ADR 0001 rule 22)

window_tokens.current_method: Every provisional or measured change of the four-account detector (`four_accounts`) opens a regime at its own instant; nothing else does, and a candidate never does. A regime opened by a provisional change is a provisional level (`provisional`). Each regime is measured in the family actually in use: its regime family is the family with the most pure clean stretches starting in it (`regime_family`, `n_regime_family`). Regimes joined by a change whose five-hour size holds no change form one run, and a run of two or more whose pure clean stretches hold 5 readings of its most common family is stated by that one cluster (`unmeasured_boundary_run_cluster`). Otherwise a regime with 5 readings is their median tokens per 1% times 100 (`measured_value`, no rate in it); below that it is the previous regime times the change's five-hour size where that size excludes no change (`previous_regime_scaled_by_known_date_change`), else the previous regime carried (`previous_regime_carried_fit_not_separable`). The published value is the newest regime's. Every earlier regime's `value` is then the next one's over the detector's five-hour size at the change between them (carried where that size holds no change), so the chart's every step is the detector's own figure; the regime's own reading stays as `own_value`. Changes applied: from 2026-09-14T09:00:00+00:00, five-hour carried; from 2026-09-23T13:00:00+00:00, five-hour +20.4%; from 2026-10-09T16:00:00+00:00, five-hour +17%.
window_tokens.family_values_method: `family_value` and `family_interval` on each regime are its window in `measured_family` tokens: the regime's own direct figure where it was measured in that family, else its anchor-unit figure over `per_family[measured_family].history_rate`.
window_tokens.method: median over the pure-opus clean stretches of the tokens the stretch carried per 1% of the five-hour meter, times 100, taken per token class and over all four classes together -- `all` over the newest regime (`current_method`), `per_class` over the whole cluster, and both sides of the newest measured change published beside each. The interval is the spread of the readings themselves -- per account its own lowest and highest per-stretch value, pooled the union of the account intervals -- and not a confidence interval. No credit rate and no class weight enters the pure-opus figure: it is the stretch's own token counts over its own meter movement. Every other family is a conversion of it at the two families' rates (`conversion`), and a family whose rate is a status sentence publishes no number. A regime after a measured change is measured the same way in its own regime family (`measured_family`, `current_method`), and that family's row is its direct reading.

fable.conversion: the Opus window tokens times the Opus input rate over the measured Fable input rate, at the same token-class mix (`per_class` above, cache reads at the published cache-read weight); the interval combines the window interval with the rate interval.

haiku.conversion: the Opus window tokens times the Opus input rate over the inferred Haiku input rate, at the same token-class mix (`per_class` above, cache reads at the published cache-read weight); the interval combines the window interval with the rate interval.

history_rate.source: derived: the rate that makes the step at 2026-10-09T16:00:00+00:00 equal the five-hour change the detector measured there (+17.0%): the previous regime's opus window times that change, over the regime's direct opus-5-5 window; its interval is the same over the regime's highest and lowest reading

sonnet.conversion: the Opus window tokens times the Opus input rate over the measured Sonnet input rate, at the same token-class mix (`per_class` above, cache reads at the published cache-read weight); the interval combines the window interval with the rate interval.

window_tokens.per_regime_method: The regimes are the window's own (`regimes`): one per provisional or measured change of the four-account detector (`four_accounts`), and none anywhere else; a row opened by a provisional change its chart draws is flagged `provisional` (the week) and `windows_per_week_provisional`. `per_week_regimes` states each regime's week directly on the seven-day meter: the credits per 1% of the seven-day meter (`weekly_credits_per_pct`), from every one-point seven-day step of every account lying wholly in the regime (`weekly_meter.seven_day_steps`, tiled between exact crossings; harness runs, cloud sessions and steps over stretches the capture check withheld out, the personal account from 6 September), each step's own tokens valued as `across_cut` values a stretch, pooled meter-weighted (every account's credits over every account's seven-day points), times 100, in the window's tokens through the anchor's credits per token at the published mix (`anchor_credits_per_token`). Its interval resamples each account's whole UTC days. No fitted coefficient enters it. Rows either side of a change whose seven-day size holds no change state one week, over the steps of both. `windows_per_week` is the week over the regime's window (`windows_per_week_source` `weekly_over_window`), its interval the week's ends over the window's opposite ends. The newest row is its own direct level. Every earlier row is restated from the one after it so each step the charts draw is the detector's own size at the change: the week by the change's seven-day size (`week_bridge`), windows per week by the ratio's (`windows_per_week_bridge`), each carried where that size holds no change; the row's direct figure stays in the bridge record. The meter ratio is published beside it for reference only: `windows_per_week_meters`, five-hour over seven-day points in the same steps, and `windows_per_week_pooled`, five-hour over seven-day movement pooled over every account's `weekly_windows.max20.by_window` readings in the regime, with its rounding interval, both with each step's or window's five-hour points over its headless inflation (ADR 0001 rule 16), the meter's own beside them as `raw_windows_per_week_meters` and `raw_windows_per_week_pooled`. `per_week` is the newest regime's figure, and every family's week moves from its window the way the anchor's does. `account_regimes` gives each account's own figures in each regime and never another account's: its week from its own steps the same way (`per_week`), its window, and `windows_per_week` its week over its window. Its window, in anchor units, is the regime's window times the account's median credits per 1% of the five-hour meter over its own clean stretches lying wholly in the regime, any family, valued as `across_cut` values them, over the same median pooled across every account's such stretches (`n_window` the account's count), so the rates only weigh sessions against each other inside one regime and the pool's median account sits at the regime's window. `measured_window` is the account's direct reading beside it: the median tokens per 1% times 100 of its own pure stretches of the regime's `regime_family` (named on the row as `measured_family`, counted in `n_measured_window`), with no rate in it, published from 5 such stretches as a regime's own direct window is (null below that: one stretch reads its own token mix, not the account's level). For regimes stated by one run's cluster, both medians are over the stretches lying wholly in the run, and every regime of the run carries the same readings. `windows_per_week_meters` is its own five-hour over seven-day readings, for reference. A figure with no reading behind it is null, and so is anything derived from it.

regimes.bridge_rate_source: derived: the rate that makes the step at 2026-09-23T13:00:00+00:00 equal the five-hour change the detector measured there (+20.4%): the previous regime's opus window times that change, over the regime's direct opus-5-5 window; its interval is the same over the regime's highest and lowest reading

derived: the rate that makes the step at 2026-10-09T16:00:00+00:00 equal the five-hour change the detector measured there (+17.0%): the previous regime's opus window times that change, over the regime's direct opus-5-5 window; its interval is the same over the regime's highest and lowest reading

window_tokens.selection: A stretch counts when it moved the meter at least 3%, carries tokens, does not overlap one of the tracker's own runs on its own account (a probe row or the effort-matrix run), and reads capture_status 'accepted'. The Max account 1 counts from 6 September, as its seven-day steps do.

five_hour_meter.method: The five-hour meter's factor for headless `claude -p` work, measured at every publish from the one-point seven-day steps (`weekly_meter.seven_day_steps`, cleaned as the weekly limit cleans them): a quasi-Poisson regression of the five-hour points crossed in each step on regime (the 14 September cut and every family's first use), account and the step's headless share of credits, where headless means a `claude -p` run's own turns (entrypoint `sdk-cli`, sub-agents not counted). `value` is exp of the share's coefficient, the five-hour meter's movement per credit of headless work over interactive work; its interval is 1.96 standard errors with the fit's own dispersion. `per_account` is the same fit on each account alone. Every five-hour figure (the window, the five-hour change tests, the account lines) counts a stretch's headless tokens at this factor, so it is quoted in interactive-equivalent tokens and credits; the seven-day meter, which treats both kinds of work alike, is not weighted. An account whose collector recorded no headless split is counted as recorded, unweighted.

headless_factor.fit: quasi-Poisson of each step's five-hour points on account x ISO-week levels and its headless share of credits

line_names.five_hour: five-hour meter: credits per 1%, headless work at the fitted factor
line_names.ratio: five-hour points per seven-day point, headless work at the fitted factor

all_four_accounts_voting.starts: October, when all four accounts had readings on both sides

sensitivity.method: a step injected into every account's real readings at every six-hour start, the rule run 7 or 14 days later with its own sides; a hit is a flag within a day of the start, in the right direction

whole_history.starts: 12 September to 15 October; in September at most two accounts voted

whole_run_false_alarms.note: histories with every account's readings shifted in time by its own random offset, the two lines searched: 2 of 20 with the 9 October ratio step left in as noise, 0 of 20 with it divided out. The 7-day hold is what keeps such a flag from becoming measured

four_accounts.sentence: Each Max account is its own ruler: when every account gets the same percentage more or less work per 1% of a meter at the same moment, and shuffling their days cannot make a jump that big more than once in a thousand tries, the limit changed.

valuation.rule: each family at the rates in force (history/model-rates.json, the pooled fit's point estimates, cache reads at its one fitted cache-read rate), except Opus 5.5, held at Anthropic's list ratio 0.8x Opus (ADR 0001 rule 23), the same rates across the whole history, so no dated regime enters a line; the ratio reads no rate but a step's headless share; each family's rate interval widens the sizes it moves (rate_dependence)

last_change.line: five-hour points per seven-day point, headless work at the fitted factor

caveats: Some Opus sessions run at about 2.5 times the model's usual speed, with nothing in between. A request in a session whose running median speed is 1.6 times the model's median or more is a fast-session request. They are real measured speeds and are included in every figure, so a day with many of them shows as a jump in the line; fast_session_requests counts them. Why these sessions run faster is not known.

a1 is one machine's transcripts; a2 to a4 are another machine's. Compare accounts and entrypoints (cli is interactive Claude Code, sdk-cli is claude -p, sdk-ts and sdk-py are the Agent SDK) with like, using by_account_entrypoint.
Time to first block includes writing the whole first block, which may be a long thinking or tool block, so it is not a time to first token.
Older days come from a stored history: Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days, so a day is computed while its transcripts exist and then kept as it was.
speed.method: Each request is timed from Claude Code's transcripts: from the last user line (a prompt or a tool result) written before the response, to the response's last content block. Output speed is the response's output tokens over that time, so it includes waiting in the queue and reading the input; it is a speed as a Claude Code user sees it, not the model's raw decoding speed. Only responses of at least 300 output tokens taking between 1 and 900 seconds are counted, and a day is shown only with at least 30 of them. Figures are the median and interquartile range across requests, per UTC day, pooled from speeds binned 2% apart. Input speed is shown as the median time from that user line to the end of the response's first block, not as a rate. A robust fit of each request's duration against its uncached input and output tokens, per model and day, gave an input rate whose 80% interval was under 1.5 times end to end on only 6 of 87 model-days with 300 or more requests (13 had no upper bound, the median was 2.7 times), and the six tight ones disagreed with each other several-fold. Claude Code sends little uncached input per request (a median of about 1,200 tokens), so the time spent reading it is lost in queueing and output time.

weekly_window_ratios_basis.scope: five-hour windows per week, relative to max20

max20.regimes_method: one regime per span between the four-account detector's provisional and measured changes (a span opened by a provisional one flagged `provisional`), pooled over every account's windows ending in it; every step the ratio's size at the change (own level in `own_windows`)
max20.unit_method: Windows per week in interactive-equivalent units (ADR 0001 rule 16): each five-hour meter window's movement (`raw_five_hour_pct`) over its headless inflation, 1 + (factor - 1) x the window's headless share of credits, with the factor fitted at this publish (`five_hour_meter.headless_factor`). The share is read from the account's seven-day steps that overlap the window's five hours, each counted by the part of its span inside them, valued as the factor's own fit values them; a window no step overlaps reads the stretches the same way; a window neither overlaps (`headless_share` null) is counted as recorded, unweighted. `five_hour_pct`, `windows` and `rounding_interval` are in that unit; the meter's own figures are kept as `raw_five_hour_pct`, `raw_windows` and `raw_rounding_interval`, a diagnostic. The seven-day meter is not weighted.
